## Pull request overview

Adds missing unit/integration tests across `@object-ui/permissions`, `@object-ui/mobile`, and `@object-ui/auth` to bring Vitest coverage back above CI thresholds.

**Changes:**
- Added permissions tests covering evaluator, store, provider/hooks, and guard behaviors.
- Added mobile tests covering responsive hooks/components plus PWA manifest and service worker registration logic.
- Added auth tests covering forms and `UserMenu` behavior via `AuthCtx.Provider` mocking.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 15 out of 15 changed files in this pull request and generated 8 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/permissions/src/__tests__/store.test.ts | Adds coverage for permission store creation and dynamic updates. |
| packages/permissions/src/__tests__/evaluator.test.ts | Adds coverage for RBAC evaluation and condition operators. |
| packages/permissions/src/__tests__/PermissionProvider.test.tsx | Adds coverage for provider + permission hooks integration and defaults. |
| packages/permissions/src/__tests__/PermissionGuard.test.tsx | Adds coverage for hide/disable/custom fallback modes. |
| packages/mobile/src/__tests__/useTouchTarget.test.ts | Adds coverage for touch target sizing defaults and overrides. |
| packages/mobile/src/__tests__/useResponsiveConfig.test.ts | Adds coverage for responsive config resolution (columns/order/hidden). |
| packages/mobile/src/__tests__/useResponsive.test.ts | Adds coverage for responsive value resolution. |
| packages/mobile/src/__tests__/useBreakpoint.test.ts | Adds coverage for breakpoint state and resize handling. |
| packages/mobile/src/__tests__/serviceWorker.test.ts | Adds coverage for service worker registration happy-path and error handling. |
| packages/mobile/src/__tests__/pwa.test.ts | Adds coverage for PWA manifest generation defaults and icon mapping. |
| packages/mobile/src/__tests__/ResponsiveContainer.test.tsx | Adds coverage for conditional rendering by breakpoint rules. |
| packages/auth/src/__tests__/UserMenu.test.tsx | Adds coverage for authenticated rendering, avatar/initials, and actions. |
| packages/auth/src/__tests__/RegisterForm.test.tsx | Adds coverage for registration validation, submission, and error handling. |
| packages/auth/src/__tests__/LoginForm.test.tsx | Adds coverage for login rendering, submission, loading, and error handling. |
| packages/auth/src/__tests__/ForgotPasswordForm.test.tsx | Adds coverage for forgot-password success and error flows. |
</details>

Several tests here rely on happy-dom’s default breakpoint being `lg` (via the default `window.innerWidth`). This can become flaky if the test environment changes. Set `window.innerWidth` explicitly for each scenario (and restore afterward) so the `showOn`/`hideOn`/`minBreakpoint` expectations don’t depend on implicit defaults.

This test mutates `navigator.serviceWorker` via `Object.defineProperty` but doesn’t restore the original descriptor afterward, which can leak state into subsequent tests (in this file or others) depending on test ordering. Capture the original descriptor in `beforeEach` and restore it in `afterEach` (or restore within each test) to keep globals isolated.

The test name suggests row-level permissions are evaluated against the provided `record`, but `evaluatePermission` currently only checks whether any `rowPermissions` entry includes the action and never evaluates the filter/record match (it only returns `rowFilter`). Either tighten the assertion to what the function actually does (e.g., that `rowFilter` is returned when rowPermissions exist), or—if row filters are meant to be enforced—add an assertion that would fail until the evaluator implements record/filter evaluation.

The `createAuthContext`/`renderWithAuth` helpers are duplicated across multiple auth test files in this PR. Consider extracting them into a shared test utility (e.g. `packages/auth/src/__tests__/testUtils.tsx`) to reduce repeated boilerplate and keep future AuthContext shape changes from requiring edits in several files.

The "responds to window resize" test doesn’t actually verify the debounced resize behavior. `useBreakpoint` updates width via a 100ms `setTimeout`, but the test never advances timers and only asserts `breakpoint` is defined (which is already true before the resize). Make this deterministic by using fake timers (advance by 100ms) and assert `result.current.width`/`breakpoint` changes after the resize event.
